Election officials review them later, and they count only if the voter's eligibility is confirmed.. What are provisional ballots? Mississippi Senate count, Nov. 2026. Provisional ballots are ballots cast by voters whose eligibility is not confirmed at the polling place, so they are set aside and checked before they are counted. In Mississippi, where they are called affidavit ballots, election officials are reviewing thousands of them in the close Senate race between Democrat Scott Colom and Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.. The Mississippi Senate race remains close while election officials review thousands of provisional ballots, and both parties have sent lawyers and observers to monitor the count.. Voters usually cast a provisional ballot when their name is missing from the poll book or when they lack the required photo identification. Officials then verify the voter's registration or identity before the ballot is added to the count. Mississippi uses the term affidavit ballot for the same category. Colom holds a very narrow lead over Hyde-Smith, and the state has not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in nearly 40 years. The Mississippi Republican Party said it sent more than 50 volunteer attorneys and observers across the state, while the NAACP deployed volunteers to all 82 counties to monitor the review. Voters who lacked identification were urged to bring the proper documents to the county courthouse. The review matters now because the outcome could decide the size of the Democratic majority in the Senate next year. Tuesday was the deadline for voters to resolve identification problems on provisional ballots, and counties must certify their results by November 13. Mississippi's state certification deadline is December 3.
